what_happened: Live re-measurement found the reported 0.66 tok/s was an outlier, not the steady state: historical llama-server print_timing lines on this machine show a consistent baseline of ~9-13 tok/s prompt-eval and ~5.5-7.7 tok/s decode-eval across many Sapience sync chunks, and a fresh controlled /api/generate call just after the slow event reproduced 6.99 tok/s decode / 28.7 tok/s prompt-eval (cold load). This reframes the task from 'inference is categorically broken' to 'baseline is already several-fold below the published HX 370 CPU reference (~80-90 tok/s pp512, ~12-15 tok/s tg for 8B Q4_K_M), plus one further transient collapse on top of that baseline.'

Ruled out the two cleanest candidate causes named in the task description: (1) generic/CPU-feature-poor llama.cpp build -- the nixpkgs ollama 0.32.3 derivation ships per-microarch libggml-cpu-{zen4,icelake,sapphirerapids,...}.so variants with runtime dispatch, and journalctl confirms AVX2/AVX512/AVX512_VNNI/AVX512_BF16/REPACK all detected true; (2) inflated context size -- n_ctx is capped at 4096 (not the model's 131072 training context) and prompt token counts per chunk were 250-440, nowhere near the cap. Neither explains the slowdown.

Found a latent, separate throttle in the Sapience vendor client (~/.sapience/extract_local.py ollama_num_thread(), comment references 'Ari Sklar #12, 2026-09-19'): the scheduled --sync path (SYNC and not BACKFILL) defaults num_thread to 1 deliberately so a background cron-style run never takes every core; only an interactive run or --backfill gets Ollama's own default (unset/0, effectively all cores). This is unrelated to the measured 0.66 tok/s event (that event's own llama-server log line shows n_threads_batch=24, i.e. not single-threaded) but must be accounted for before treating any local-sync throughput number as representative, and would need a deliberate override (SAPIENCE_NUM_THREAD or config.json num_thread) if local sync inference is ever made the default path.
